document.title: Danas Piano Tutor — technical status
document.maintainer_note: Hand-maintained. Update 'status' when features change and append to 'changelog' for every change; the repository has no git history, so this file is the record.

product.name: Danas Piano Tutor
product.purpose: Scripted lessons for entry-level piano students: build a simple piece as text, listen at any speed with a metronome, see hand and finger positions, and print the sheet music.

known_limitations: No beams: eighth and sixteenth notes are drawn with flags.
Up to two voices per hand are engraved with stems; extra voices are dropped with a warning.
No triplets, grace notes, dynamics, slurs, pedal or repeat signs.
One hand position model (five white keys); black-key positions are not modelled.
Clef and rest glyphs come from the system font (Segoe UI Symbol on Windows); other platforms fall back to drawn shapes.
The `.py` file association on the development machine points at Python 3.1 — use the .bat or `py -3.14`.

architecture.principle: A lesson is data on a division grid (8 per quarter). Audio, keyboard, hands, score, PDF and MusicXML are all derived from that one model; nothing is stored twice.

changelog.summary: A metronome the microphone does not hear as a note
changes: raw/teach/voice.py: click(accent, unpitched) — a high noise burst (high-passed at 3.6 kHz, 2.6 kHz accented) for when the microphone is listening; a sine click reads as a note (F#6, clarity 0.97) and raising its pitch would only move the detection to a sub-harmonic.
PlayOptions.metronome_unpitched, threaded through web_api.render and the transport; Practice switches to it with the piano mute.

listen/pitch.js: reject a window that is near-silent where YIN looks but loud at its end (a click's attack), which used to read as a confident note — the frames before each click reported an ascending scale.
Measured with the real detector over a rendered metronome track: 23 frames read as a pitch with the ordinary click, 0 with the practice click; rendered C3/C4/C5 still detected in every frame.
Tests: TestPracticeMetronome (3 cases, YIN clarity measured in numpy); suite 442.

changelog.summary: Practice runs: listen, play along, on your own
changes: web/src/run.js: the three passes, passAt() for locating a time in the run, buildRunSamples() for assembling one buffer, and the end-of-run summary.

Transport.prepareRun() renders the full mix and the metronome-only mix and builds a three-pass buffer (pass 3 = the metronome mix with everything after the count-in zeroed); playRun() plays it and reports each pass through onRunPass.
Every pass gets a bar of count-in clicks, so the change of pass is unmistakable and all three passes are the same length.
Passes 2 and 3 are scored as separate attempts and compared at the end: score, notes, tempo drift, and a sentence on what the pair means.
ranking.js: tempo drift by fitting the timing error against the beat it fell on, reported in bpm.
Practice panel: Run button, a live three-pass banner with scores, the comparison card; also in the Ctrl+K palette. Without a microphone the run still plays as a guided drill, unscored.

changelog.summary: The metronome no longer stops between the passes of a run
changes: Each render ends with a tail of silence for the last note's release; laying the three renders end to end put that tail between the passes, so the beat stopped for 0.35 s at every change of pass (a pass measured 16.583 beats instead of 16).
A pass is now exactly its count-in plus its section, and the renders are mixed in at their pass positions, so a release rings on over the next pass's count-in instead of delaying it.
Measured: 9.6 s per pass at 100 bpm, exactly 16 beats, no click more than 0.2 ms from its beat across the boundary.

changelog.summary: Listen no longer sounds silent
changes: The practice click was inaudible: band-passing the noise at 3.2 kHz threw away its energy, leaving it 16 dB below the ordinary click A-weighted while the piano was muted at the same time. It is now lightly high-passed (1.2 kHz, 0.9 kHz accented) with 6 dB of make-up gain in the player — measured A-weighted, ordinary -4.4 dB against practice -4.8 dB, with YIN clarity still 0.33.

Ticking Listen muted the piano in every mode, including Learn where the point is to hear the piece. The mute now applies only in Practice, where the microphone is scored; the unpitched click is used whenever the microphone is open.

Verified in the browser: Learn with Listen on renders at peak 0.74 with the piano; Practice at peak 0.67 with the click alone and zero frames read as a note; in a run every count-in peaks at 0.67 and pass 3's section is exactly silent.
The test now asserts what matters: the practice click is within 3 dB of the ordinary one A-weighted, and never reaches the detector's clarity threshold.

changelog.summary: Phone layouts, portrait and landscape
changes: Portrait (<=640 px): the rail becomes a bottom bar; the panel is a sheet over the stage, closed by default and raised when there is something to read; the transport takes its own row above the keyboard and scrolls sideways.
Landscape (<=520 px tall): icon-only rail, tighter bands, panel as a side sheet; the staff keeps about half the height.

The keyboard chooses its octave count so a white key stays at least ~26 px wide, centred on the music; the score chooses its staff size from the width (5 px per staff space on a phone against 8 on a desktop). Both recompute on resize and orientation change.
Touch: 40 px targets under (pointer: coarse), 100dvh so browser chrome cannot hide the keyboard, viewport-fit=cover and safe-area insets for notched phones.

Fixed a canvas bug this uncovered, which affected every HiDPI screen: the backing store's height attribute counts as a specified height and beat the inset:0 stretch, so canvases were laid out at devicePixelRatio size — twice as tall as their box on a phone. setupCanvas now writes the CSS size explicitly.

changelog.summary: Say why Practice goes quiet, and let the piano back in
changes: Muting the piano while the microphone is scored is deliberate, but it reads as a fault: measured over 8 s of playback, Practice with Listen on carries sound in 12 of 149 frames (the clicks) against 94 in Learn. It now says so in the status line.

Practice panel: 'Play the piano too' for anyone on headphones — 87 of 151 frames with it on — warning that the microphone will otherwise hear the piano and flatter the score. Remembered in the browser.
The AudioContext watches its own state and resumes itself: opening a microphone can make the browser change output device, which interrupts the context and would otherwise stop playback for good.

New 'Sound check' command: plays a tone through the normal output and reports the level a meter on that output saw, separating a silent app from a silent system (Windows quietens other sounds while a microphone is open).

changelog.summary: Choose where the tutor plays, and notice when the system moves it
changes: Opening a microphone on Windows commonly moves playback to the communications device (a headset, or a virtual device such as NVIDIA Broadcast), so the app plays into something nobody is listening to — the usual reason a page goes silent when a microphone opens.
The default output is read before the microphone opens and again after; a change is reported in the status line.
Set up carries a 'Sound out' picker (AudioContext.setSinkId) that pins playback to a chosen device, remembered in the browser, with a Test button beside it.

changelog.summary: Practice plays everything again; nothing above the lesson is registered
changes: The piano is no longer muted when Listen is ticked: piano and metronome play together in Practice as they do in Learn (87 of 151 frames carrying sound, against 12 when muted). Muting survives as an opt-in switch for players without headphones, since the microphone hears the tutor too and a score counts what it hears.
Listener.ceilingMidi: nothing above the lesson's top note plus four semitones is registered as a note, so the metronome — and the room — cannot become one.

Tried and rejected: a tonal click above the notes. A single sine is found at once, raising it moves the find to a sub-harmonic, and two partials beat against each other (2637 + 3349 Hz reads as E5 at clarity 0.91). The click stays noise, which has no period to find (clarity 0.33) and is measured level with the ordinary click A-weighted.

changelog.summary: Stop the app hanging at "Loading…" behind a stale cache
changes: The service worker treated core.zip as immutable alongside the pinned Pyodide release, but core.zip is the whole Python core and is rebuilt with every change — a returning visitor ran yesterday's Python behind today's JavaScript. Only vendor/ is cache-first now.

Bridge.fail(): when the worker dies, everything waiting on it is rejected instead of hanging for ever; the app waits on parse before it can show a lesson, so a dead worker used to leave the title at 'Loading…' with no explanation.
Bridge.boot() gives the runtime 90 seconds and then says so, and a failed boot writes the reason on the splash rather than the status bar, which can be off the bottom of the screen.

changelog.summary: Know which build you are looking at
changes: Every build is stamped with the commit it came from and the time it was made (GITHUB_SHA under Actions, git in a working copy, '+' when dirty); the stamp is written into about.json and precache.json.
The stamp is shown on the welcome screen and in Set up: version, build, and when it was built.

The page compares its own stamp with the server's precache.json — on load, when the tab is focused, and from 'Check for a newer build' — and shows 'Update ready — reload' in the top bar when a newer one is live, naming both builds.
